### Observed differences

- In the earlier window, A19, A21, A22 and A23 each ran in about 20–28 of 100 cases, essentially never two of them in the same case, so together they covered virtually every case; in the later window each of the four appears in only about 1–2 of 100 cases. [OCC002, OCC004, OCC005, OCC006, REL024, REL040, REL047]
- In the earlier window, A20, A28, A29 and A30 were observed in at most 1 of 200 cases; in the later window each of them runs in about 98–99 of 100 cases, any pair of them co-occurs in about 98–99 of 100 cases, and their mutual order is mixed (for example A20 precedes A28 in about 45 of 100 cases and A28 precedes A20 in about 52 of 100). [OCC003, OCC007, OCC008, OCC009, REL035, REL056, REL060]
- The swap sits between A46 and A31, which themselves ran in essentially every case in both windows: in the earlier window A46's outgoing traffic went to A19 (about 26%), A21 (25%), A22 (28%) and A23 (20%), each of which led almost exclusively to A31; in the later window A46's outgoing traffic goes to A29 (about 26%), A30 (24%), A28 (23%) and A20 (19%) instead, and each of the four is followed by any of the other three and by A31. [DIR011, DIR003, DIR005, DIR006, DIR007, DIR004, DIR008, DIR009, DIR010]
- In the later window A46 precedes A20, A28, A29 and A30 in about 97–98 of 100 cases, and each of the four precedes A31 in about 97–98 of 100 cases; the measured gap from A46 to A31 moved from about 2 steps (97 of 100 earlier cases) to the 5-steps-or-more category (98 of 100 later cases), and A31 itself now occurs later in the case (mean position about 0.40 to 0.46). [REL038, REL039, REL058, REL059, REL061, REL062, REL063, REL064, LAG003, POS012]
- A14 precedes the new activities in about 98 of 100 later cases, whereas before it preceded A19, A21 or A22 only in the roughly 25–28 of 100 cases in which those ran; A15 co-occurs with the new activities in about 98 of 100 later cases but without a fixed order (A15 first in about 55 of 100, interleaved in about 44 of 100). [REL009, REL010, REL013, REL015, REL017, REL020]
- A06 participation halved, from about 27 to about 14 of 100 cases, and when it occurs it now sits later and more variably in the case (mean position about 0.19 to 0.39); its outgoing traffic spread from mostly A15 (about 89%) to A15 (43%) plus many successors, and the share of A14's outgoing transitions going to A06 fell from about 25% to 6%. [OCC001, POS001, DIR001, DIR002]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the hypothesis that the segment between A46 and A31 was restructured: in the earlier window each case executed exactly one of A19, A21, A22 and A23 there, as mutually exclusive alternatives each leading to A31 within about two steps, whereas in the later window cases execute A20, A28, A29 and A30 together, in mixed order, in that same segment — A46 precedes the four in about 97–98 of 100 cases, the four precede A31 in about 97–98 of 100 cases, and the A46-to-A31 distance stretched from about 2 steps to 5 or more. About 100 evidence items qualified against roughly 1 expected if nothing had changed, and the occurrence, routing, ordering and distance indicators all point to the same placement, which the relational items show directly. [OCC002, OCC003, OCC004, OCC005, OCC006, OCC007, OCC008, OCC009, DIR011, REL035, REL038, REL039, REL058, REL061, REL063, LAG003]

Limitations: zero participation in the earlier window shows only that A20, A28, A29 and A30 were not observed there — if they existed at all before, they ran in well under about 2 of 100 cases — and the later outgoing profiles of A19, A21, A22 and A23 rest on only 2–4 observations each. Many relation items re-describe the same swap from different activity pairs, so they are not independent confirmations. A competing explanation the evidence cannot rule out is that the two windows draw on different case populations, so the swap could reflect which cases were sampled rather than a modified single process; positions are event positions, so no clock-time timing claim is implied. [OCC003, OCC007, OCC008, OCC009, DIR003, DIR005, DIR006, DIR007]

Other differences: A06 participation halved (about 27 to about 14 of 100 cases), it occurs later and more variably when present, its outgoing traffic spread from mostly A15 to many successors, and A14 → A06 fell to about 6% of A14's outgoing; A14, A15 and A46 each occur slightly earlier (mean-position drops of about 0.01–0.03). The evidence does not show whether A06's change belongs to the same restructuring. [OCC001, POS001, DIR001, DIR002, POS002, POS003, POS013]
